description: Borromean per-braid tower net/target vs canonical sgn(w₀)·dim; A-scaling diagnostic + edge-set test + extensive-bulk comparison (no fit, no closure).

edge_set_test.note: sparsifying the edge set (all-pairs C(A,2)~A² → adjacent A−1~A) WORSENS the spread (monotone under-bind at heavy A) — the U-shape is NOT a pure edge-count effect; it is A²-overscaling at the heavy end PLUS the ⁴He magic dip (no shell structure). Edge-set lever (w5tg) alone is insufficient; the per-pair magnitude (~0.4 MeV) is far below ~8 MeV/nucleon, so closure needs magnitude-reshaping (z2bn R(q,x)) + shell/magic structure, not sparsification.

extensive_bulk.note: the extensive A-linear 2·m_e·8G (≈7.49 MeV/nucleon ≈ empirical ~8) gives net/target 0.85–1.06 for A≥4 (spread 1.65×) — FAR flatter than the tower's A² pair structure (6.17×). The BULK binding is extensive (A-linear shell residue), NOT a q-deformed pair sum; the tower's C(A,2)~A² scaling is the q-Gaussian obstruction (Σ q₀^cr(π) ~ q₀^C(A,2) diverges at q₀>1, prop:q-gaussian-obstruction-at-q0). q-Askey kernels (Hahn-Exton q-Bessel / q-Hermite) are the FIBRE per-λ kernel (|q|≤1), not the A-scaling bulk.
